query: Reported superconducting high-entropy alloys are dominated by Nb-Ta matrices, while other studies concern titanium-rich systems based on heavy transition metals and partly ordered systems. Consequently, these precedents do not establish what controls superconductivity in high-entropy alloys outside the best-studied material classes. Within the defining constraint of a solid solution containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each, what governs superconducting behavior in such an uncharacterized high-entropy alloy, and why? State one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison against the starting material, predicted observations relative to the baseline, applicable boundary conditions, the earlier evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In a single-phase high-entropy alloy (HEA) superconductor, the superconducting transition temperature (T_c) is governed primarily by the average valence electron concentration per atom (VEC), because VEC controls the electronic density of states at the Fermi level and thus the electron–phonon coupling strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic, single-phase HEA composed of five transition metals (e.g. Re0.2Mo0.2W0.2Ta0.2Zr0.2) with VEC≈4.8.
generation.intervention: Systematically substitute 10 at.% Zr with Ti to raise the average VEC (e.g. Re0.2Mo0.2W0.2Ta0.2Zr0.1Ti0.1, VEC≈4.9) while retaining a single-phase solid solution.
generation.conditions: Arc‐melting and homogenization at 1200 °C under identical annealing schedules, measurements taken at ambient pressure.
generation.structural_mediator: Substitution increases average electron count without inducing phase separation, slightly contracts lattice parameter and stiffens phonon modes.
generation.mechanism: Higher VEC raises the electronic density of states at the Fermi level and enhances electron–phonon coupling constant λ, yielding a higher T_c.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Ti‐substituted HEA will exhibit a T_c ~0.3–0.7 K higher than the baseline equiatomic alloy.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic Re0.2Mo0.2W0.2Ta0.2Zr0.2 HEA with measured T_c0.
generation.boundary: Holds only for single‐phase, disordered solid solutions with no significant chemical ordering or second‐phase formation; VEC variation ≤0.2.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate uncertainty in magnitude of T_c shift (±0.2 K) due to possible changes in phonon spectrum not fully captured by VEC alone.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two HEA samples: baseline Re0.2Mo0.2W0.2Ta0.2Zr0.2 and the Ti‐substituted Re0.2Mo0.2W0.2Ta0.2Zr0.1Ti0.1. Verify single‐phase by XRD, measure T_c via four‐probe resistivity and specific heat.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Ti‐substituted alloy shows no increase (or a decrease) in T_c beyond experimental uncertainty (±0.2 K), or if γ does not increase in proportion to VEC, then the hypothesis is falsified.
